the performance of loop scheduling algorithms for multiprocessors is signi cantly a ected by the location of data in the memory system, that traditional scheduling algorithms that ignore the location of the data can incur a performance penalty as large as a factor of on some multiprocessors, and that a new algorithm that attempts to co locate data and loop iterations improves performance by up to a factor on some multiprocessor workstations.
loop scheduling algorithms that ignore the location of the data can incur a signi cance performance penalty on shared memory multipro cessors

traditional algorithms for scheduling loops on shared memory multipro cessors ignore the location of loop data, which can cause substantial performance degradations in modern shared memory multipro cessors, that we propose a new algorithm which attempts to minimize communication overhead by scheduling loops to co-locate loop data, that the new algorithm out performs the traditional algorithms in all cases, and that this performance improvement is substantial in some cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of scheduling loops on multiprocessor shared memory machines Our goal is to minimize execution time by distributing the loop iterations evenly among processors while minimizing the number synchronization and communication overheads We present a novel approach that takes into account the location of data as well as the location of processors in the scheduling decision making process Our results show that the proposed scheduling algorithm outperforms other known scheduling techniques by up to a factor in some cases on several multiprocessors including the Silicon Graphics multiprocessors the BBN

the problem of scheduling parallel loops in shared memory multiprocessor architectures We have proposed a new algorithm for loop scheduling that attempts to minimize the amount of communication incurred by parallelizing loops We have implemented our algorithm and compared its performance to other known algorithms on a number of representative parallel programs We show that our algorithm o ers a signi cant speedup over other scheduling algorithms and that the performance di erences between the scheduling algorithms are substantial

the problem of scheduling loop iterations on a multiprocessor system with distributed memory We have developed a new loop scheduling scheme called processor a nity scheduling that attempts to minimize communication costs in addition to minimizing synchronization and load balancing costs Our experimental results demonstrate that this scheme can provide substantial performance improvements over other loop scheduling schemes
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed algorithm is a very good solution to the scheduling problem in shared memory multiprocessor environments, but that it is not the best possible solution, as it does not consider the cache coherency protocol and the cache miss penalty.
the new algorithm performs better in most cases, but that the performance of the other algorithms is still quite good.

the proposed scheduling algorithm is the most e ective in reducing communication overhead and thus is the most e cient in reducing the execution time of a parallel loop on shared memory multiprocesors
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a new loop scheduling scheme for shared memory multiproces sors which is based on the processor affinity principle The new scheme has been shown to be very e ective in reducing communication overhead and thus improving the performance of loop based programs on shared memory multiproce ssors

we have developed an e cient and scalable algorithm for mapping loops onto shared memory multiprocessor architectures The algorithm takes advantage of both processor and memory locality to achieve a signi cant reduction in the number of cache misses incurred during the execution of the parallelized loop We show that this algorithm is superior to existing algorithms for loop parallelization in both performance and scalability on a variety of shared memory architectures

loop scheduling on shared memories is a complex issue which requires the consideration of many di erent factors such as the number of processors the amount of available data the amount of available cache memory and so on
The main takeaway from our work is that
data locality is important in shared memory multiprocessor scheduling and that it is important to consider it when scheduling loop iterations
the location of data relative to processors can be a major factor in determining the e ectiveness of loop scheduling algorithms

loop scheduling algorithms that ignore the location of loop iterations relative to the data that they access will incur a substantial performance penalty on modern multiprocessors This is because the cost of accessing nonlocal data has become a signi cant portion of the total cost of loop execution
